newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori denies his troops shot Lima rebels.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori denies his troops shot Lima rebels.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori on Friday denied reports that his troops had captured and then executed some of the 14 Marxist rebels slain in the assault on the Japanese ambassador's residence.
"That is completely false. There were no executions," Fujimori told Reuters in his first interview since Tuesday's daring military strike to end the 126-day hostage crisis.

He said that five of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels died in the initial explosion, while five others including leader Nestor Cerpa died rushing up a staircase. The other four lost their lives while fighting troops in the upper story, he said.

Asked if the troops had an order to kill and take no prisoners, Fujimori replied: "The order and the objective was to free the 72 hostages, not one less. We achieved freeing 72 with one who died afterwards."
Persistent reports from military, intelligence and hostage sources have said two guerrillas were shot after being captured and that at least one more begged to surrender.
The reports, in local and foreign media, have seriously undercut the acclaim that Fujimori and his armed forces won for the raid.
An army commando who took part in the operation had said that "the order was to leave no one alive. For us, the instruction was to leave no prisoners."
Fujimori said the operation was intended to last six minutes but it was complicated by a stubborn 16-minute resistance by the MRTA in the house's northern wing.

Other members of Fujimori's government seemed to be pushing hard to quash the reports of prisoner executions. Agriculture Minister Rodolfo Munante, a freed hostage, vehemently denied that he had seen or heard any of the rebels trying to surrender before they were killed.

"I have not said that at any time and it seems absolutely absurd," Munante told a news conference. He had been quoted by CBS/Telenoticias television as having described seeing a rebel surrender in the room where captive judges were held.
No one except Munante had been quoted by name as reporting executions.

At least one teenage rebel girl was also shot to death while trying to give up, an intelligence agent who monitored the raid via listening devices said. The source said the girl shouted "We surrender! We surrender!" when she was surprised along with at least one other female rebel.
Military sources said each rebel was given a final "coup de grace" shot in the forehead to make sure they were dead.

Siege leader Nestor Cerpa was shot to death as he ran up a grand staircase. He had been caught off guard playing soccer as commandos exploded through the floor and swarmed out of tunnels dug under the mansion. His last words, according to security force sources, were: "We're screwed, we're screwed."

In what looked like an extraordinary security lapse, Cerpa had allowed his fighters to put down their weapons and take off their shirts for a game of soccer in a reception hall when the troops blasted in.
An MRTA spokesman in Europe, Isaac Velazco, accused Munante of recanting his testimony about executions due to pressure from the government.

"We affirm that our comrades were repeatedly shot to finish them off by the Peruvian army and the Peruvian police," Velazco said by telephone from Hamburg, Germany. "Their practice has always been to kill our militants ... who have been captured."

All 14 rebels, one hostage and two soldiers died in the assault, which rescued 71 men after 126 days in captivity. The MRTA, widely seen as a spent force, threatened to carry out reprisal attacks in response to the military raid.
The MRTA has barely 200 fighters, mainly in the eastern jungle, and has apparently not taken any armed actions since an earlier threat on Tuesday, just hours after the attack.

Fujimori, enjoying one of Peru's greatest triumphs in a 17-year war against leftist guerrillas, toured the burned-out residence later on Thursday with visiting Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and wheelchair-bound Japanese Ambassador Morihisa Aoki, the host of the ill-fated Dec. 17 party that was seized by the MRTA.
The whereabouts of the bodies of 12 of the slain MRTA rebels remained a mystery on Friday, although Cerpa and Rojas were privately buried on Thursday night by relatives.
